findings.title: Console.warn directly exposed in core module
findings.detail: Direct console.warn() call violates dependency inversion principle. Core modules should depend on abstractions, not concrete implementations like the Console class.
findings.recommendation: Introduce Logger abstraction interface and inject via constructor. Replace console.warn with logger.warn()
findings.impact: Tests must mock console, making them fragile; harder to swap output mechanisms for different environments
findings.suggestion: Create Logger interface with warn/info/debug methods, pass instance to chunkRunner

findings.title: Optional schema field lacks explicit default contract
findings.detail: Adding status?: AgentStatus without clarifying whether this is an additive-only change or allows existing consumers to interpret null/undefined differently violates Open/Closed Principle concerns for API consumers.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit comment that existing JSON envelope contracts are unaffected, document the field's backward-compatible nature in code comments
findings.impact: Future API versioning may be impacted if semantics of null/undefined vs 'ok' diverge from expectations
findings.suggestion: Add explicit comment that existing JSON envelope contracts are unaffected, document the field's backward-compatible nature in code comments

findings.title: Mock implementation bypasses real onProgress contract verification
findings.detail: The test directly invokes onProgress with a mocked handler, which means it's not testing the integration through actual event flow. While common in unit tests, this may hide issues in how progress events compose across multiple emitters.
findings.evidence:
onProgress?.({
            phase: 'end',
            name: 'security',
            index: 1,
            total: 1,
            findings: [],
            elapsedMs: 610000,
            status: 'timeout',
          })
findings.recommendation: Consider using integration tests that exercise the full progress event composition chain rather than directly invoking emitters
findings.impact: Unit tests may not catch issues in how multiple onProgress callbacks compose their event state
findings.suggestion: Consider using integration tests that exercise the full progress event composition chain rather than directly invoking emitters

findings.title: Caught errors silently converted to status enum without logging the original exception
findings.detail: Catch block at line 521-537 catches agent execution errors, classifies them via classifyAgentError(err), and stores in agentStatus[agent.name] but never logs. The original Error object with stack trace and message is lost - only 'error' or 'timeout' string survives.
findings.impact: Production failures become black boxes - operator sees 'error' status but no error message or stack trace. Incident MTTR increases as engineers cannot diagnose what failed without reproducing the exact conditions.

findings.title: Agent status field added but no completion log on success path
findings.detail: Success paths at lines 498, 516, and 531 set status: 'ok' but never log the successful completion. Only progress events emit; there's no finalization log showing when agents complete.
findings.impact: Silent successes make it impossible to verify that agents are actually completing healthily. Only failures have any visibility through existing logs.

findings.title: Parallel agent branch catches errors without logging
findings.detail: Catch block handling parallel agent execution (lines 461-478) converts exception to status enum but loses original error context. No logger.error or console.error statements.
findings.impact: Incidents occurring only in parallel mode have no error visibility. Debugging timing-related failures or race conditions becomes impossible without the original exception details.

findings.title: Coverage agent error path loses exception context
findings.detail: Catch block for coverage agent (lines 393-405) sets status from agentStatus.coverage but never logs the caught exception. The original Error is completely lost.
findings.impact: Coverage runs silently fail without any error signal. Quality assurance cannot detect when coverage-specific issues occur because no errors are logged to observability systems.

findings.title: Parallel execution earlyExit path missing status logging
findings.detail: The parallel execution branch at lines 443-459 catches shouldStop conditions and sets status but doesn't log when an agent exits early. Early termination events aren't observable.
findings.impact: Early exits may indicate bugs or intentional behavior. Without logging, operators cannot distinguish between healthy short-circuit behavior and premature failures.

findings.title: Normal termination lacks exit log
findings.detail: The return statement after coverage success (lines 403-408) silently completes without logging. Successful normal exits have no audit trail.
findings.impact: Normal completions go unrecorded. Without success logs, you only know agents failed - you can't verify healthy run-to-run behavior or build confidence in the system.

findings.title: mergeResults has high cyclomatic complexity (CCN=22)
findings.detail: The mergeResults function at lines 127-243 has CCN of 22 and NLOC of 65, exceeding recommended thresholds. This creates complexity where multiple branch paths make the logic harder to test and maintain.
findings.evidence: mergeResults@127-243 with CCN=22 from lizard metrics showing in warnings section
findings.recommendation: Extract conditional branches into separate helper functions that each handle a specific merge scenario (tool availability, diff coverage gaps, agent skips)
findings.suggestion: Decompose into smaller functions - one for merging findings, one for collecting skipped files, one for aggregating tool status

findings.title: mergeResults has medium complexity (CCN=22)
findings.detail: The merge function continues to accumulate branches across multiple decision points. While not at critical threshold, it represents an area where complexity could further grow if additional merge scenarios are added.
findings.evidence: Lines 127-243 in chunkRunner.ts shows continued accumulation of branching logic
findings.recommendation: Consider extracting tool availability check and result filtering into separate private helpers that are each single-purpose functions
findings.suggestion: Use early return patterns to reduce nesting depth, and consider if some merge operations could happen via composition instead of conditional branches

findings.title: Main run function has very high cyclomatic complexity (CCN=63)
findings.detail: The main orchestrator function spanning lines 162-458 has CCN of 63 and NLOC of 178, which is extremely complex for a single function. This makes it difficult to understand execution flow and write comprehensive tests.
findings.evidence: (anonymous)@162-458 with CCN=63 and NLOC=178 from lizard metrics in warnings section
findings.recommendation: Split into separate functions: one for agent orchestration, one for coverage gap handling, one for parallel execution path - each with a single responsibility
findings.suggestion: Split into separate functions: one for agent orchestration, one for coverage gap handling, one for parallel execution path - each with a single responsibility

findings.title: onProgress has elevated complexity (CCN=11)
findings.detail: The onProgress callback handler at lines 295-326 has CCN of 11 with multiple conditional branches for rendering status information. While acceptable, adding more edge cases will increase this further.
findings.recommendation: Extract the status suffix generation into a separate helper function to reduce the callback's branching factor
findings.suggestion: Create dedicated formatter functions for each output component (index, name, elapsed, findings, status) rather than embedding all rendering logic in one callback
